Get Administrative Boundaries Matching INKAR

Source: R/geometry.R
get_inkar_geometry.Rd

Returns sf polygons for a spatial level with a Kennziffer column in the same format as get_inkar_data(), so the two can be joined directly. Boundaries come from Eurostat GISCO LAU (Gemeinden), whose territorial status matches INKAR. Higher levels are built by dissolving the Gemeinden; Gemeindeverbaende use the Destatis Gemeindeverzeichnis to assign each Gemeinde to its Verband.

Usage

get_inkar_geometry(
  level = c("KRE", "BND", "BLD", "GVB", "GEM"),
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

level

Character. One of "BND", "BLD", "KRE", "GVB", "GEM". "ROR" is not available.

refresh

Logical. If TRUE, ignore the cache and download again.

Value

An sf object (CRS ETRS89-LAEA, EPSG:3035) with columns Kennziffer and geometry (plus name for "GEM").

Details

The GISCO file (about 43 MB) is downloaded once and the German polygons are cached. In interactive sessions the cache persists across sessions; see clear_inkar_cache().

Source: (c) EuroGeographics for the administrative boundaries. Please keep this attribution in published maps.

Examples

# Downloads about 43 MB on first use, so it only runs interactively
if (interactive() && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)) {
  kreise <- get_inkar_geometry("KRE")
}
